para.text: The first is the screen co-ordinate system in which the positive Y direction is downwards (a relic dating from the first days of the computer). This system is used on the paintbox canvas area, where simply the rows and columns of pixels are count. A variant of this is the relative dimension used in
, where the positions relative to the paintbox dimensions (width and height) are to be entered (in integer values of %).

para.text: For plotting of graphical data in scientific applications the mathematical standard is used where the positive Y direction is upwards (for conventional 2D graphs). In XYGRAPH this system is obviously applied for the user co-ordinates. User co-ordinates are co-ordinates set by a user defined set of X and Y axes, and makes the plotting of results very convenient.
